intro: Karate and taekwondo are often mixed up on signs and in movies. They have separate histories. Karate grew on Okinawa, in the old Ryukyu Kingdom, with ideas from China. Taekwondo was built in South Korea after 1945, with a new national name.

Both arts moved from small rooms into schools, armies, universities and world federations. Wars, empires and the Olympic Games shaped them. In this unit you will follow each art from its first teachers to its first Olympic medals.
By the end, you will be able to explain where each art came from and name the people who carried it. You will also compare how karate and taekwondo got their names, ranks and rule books.
bigQuestion: How did karate and taekwondo each become an art with a national name, a school plan and a world federation?

timeline.t: Soldiers from Satsuma, in southern Japan, invade the Ryukyu Kingdom
Japan ends the Ryukyu Kingdom and makes it Okinawa Prefecture
Itosu Ankō writes ten points on karate for Okinawan schools
Japan takes over Korea as a colony
Funakoshi Gichin shows karate at a demonstration in Tokyo
Karate teachers in Naha agree to write karate as empty hand
World War II ends; Korea is freed and the U.S. rules Okinawa
The name taekwondo is chosen in Seoul
Kukkiwon opens in Seoul; Okinawa returns to Japan
Taekwondo becomes a full Olympic medal sport in Sydney
Karate appears at the Tokyo Olympics; para taekwondo joins the Paralympics

an Okinawan word meaning hand; an old name for local unarmed arts
a set pattern of movements practiced alone; karate teachers name each one
a public showing of an art or skill, not a contest with a winner
the meaning of karate as written since the 1930s
a black belt level; the system began in judo and spread to karate and taekwondo
a group that writes the rules and runs contests for a sport
a land ruled by another country
a Korean word for a hall or school; the early schools of taekwondo were each a kwan
a Korean martial art and sport; the name means roughly the way of foot and fist
taekwondo's national headquarters in Seoul, opened in 1972; it issues dan certificates

choices: an island kingdom that included Okinawa
test.why: Ryukyu was an island kingdom with its capital at Shuri, on Okinawa.

test.q: Which art grew first on Okinawa?
test.why: Karate grew on Okinawa. Taekwondo was built in Korea after 1945.

test.q: Who showed karate in Tokyo in 1922?
test.why: Funakoshi Gichin, a schoolteacher from Shuri, gave the 1922 demonstration.

test.q: What did the first written name of karate mean?
test.why: The first characters meant Tang hand, or China hand.

test.q: Why did Itosu Ankō write a letter in 1908?
choices: to explain karate's place in schools
test.why: Itosu's ten points explained karate as health and character training for schools.

test.q: When did Japan rule Korea as a colony?
What did the first kwan mostly teach?
test.why: Their founders had trained in karate, and their early lessons came from it.

test.q: Which statement compares the two arts correctly?
choices: taekwondo is older than karate by centuries
karate grew on Okinawa; taekwondo was named in Korea in 1955
test.why: Karate grew on Okinawa. The name taekwondo was chosen in Seoul in 1955.
Kukkiwon, taekwondo's headquarters in Seoul, issues dan certificates.

test.q: When did taekwondo become a full Olympic medal sport?
test.why: Taekwondo was a demonstration sport in 1988 and 1992 and a medal sport in 2000.

test.q: What did both karate and taekwondo borrow from judo?
test.why: Kanō's judo created dan ranks, which karate and then taekwondo used.

test.q: Who ruled Okinawa after World War II until 1972?
test.why: The United States ruled Okinawa from 1945 until it returned Okinawa to Japan in 1972.

test.q: Why did karate signs spread in American towns after 1945?
choices: service members trained in Okinawa and Japan and opened schools
test.why: American service members learned karate abroad and opened schools at home.

test.q: How did World Taekwondo change scoring by London 2012?
choices: it used sensors in body protectors
test.why: Electronic scoring used sensors in the body protectors at London 2012.

choices: a sport played only by children
a sport shown at the Games whose medals do not count
a sport banned from the Games
test.why: A demonstration sport is shown at the Olympics, but its medals are not official.

write.prompt: Some people call taekwondo Korean karate. Is that fair? Use at least three dates or records from this unit, such as Funakoshi's 1922 demonstration, the 1955 naming of taekwondo, Kukkiwon's 1972 opening or the Sydney 2000 Olympics. Explain what each one shows.
tips: Name each date and record you use.
Say what the first kwan teachers learned and where.
Say what changed after 1955: name, forms, rules and bodies.
Compare the two arts without ranking one above the other.
Use key words such as kwan, dan, federation and Kukkiwon.
